definitions.explanation: A person who has been captured and held, especially an enemy taken in battle. A formal, literary word now found mainly in writing, history, and translation.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}の{虜囚|りょしゅう}として{扱|あつか}われた。
examples.english: He was treated as a captive of the enemy.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{虜囚|りょしゅう}の{身|み}から、ようやく{解放|かいほう}された。
examples.english: He was finally freed after a long captivity.

notes:
A formal, somewhat literary term. In everyday speech {捕虜|ほりょ} is far more common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}となる: to become a captive
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}の{身|み}: the status of a captive
- {虜囚|りょしゅう}{生活|せいかつ}: life in captivity

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {捕虜|ほりょ}: prisoner of war — the ordinary, neutral word
- {人質|ひとじち}: hostage — held to force concessions, not captured in battle
